`Client` and `AsyncClient` both subclass `BaseClient` (httpx/_client.py:594, httpx/_client.py:1307, both extending `BaseClient` at httpx/_client.py:188).

- **`BaseClient`** (httpx/_client.py:188) holds shared, transport-agnostic logic used by both: config properties (`timeout`, `base_url`, `headers`, `cookies`, `params`, `event_hooks`, `auth`), request-building helpers (`.build_request()`, `_merge_url/_merge_cookies/_merge_headers/_merge_queryparams`), and redirect/auth bookkeeping (`_build_redirect_request`, `_build_auth`, `_redirect_method/_redirect_url/_redirect_headers`, `_enforce_trailing_slash`, `_get_proxy_map`, `_set_timeout`, `is_closed`).
- **`Client`** (httpx/_client.py:594) is the sync implementation: it adds the synchronous transport plumbing (`_transport_for_url`, `_init_transport`, `_init_proxy_transport`) and sync versions of `send`, `_send_handling_redirects`, `_send_handling_auth`, `_send_single_request`, `stream`, the verb methods (`get/post/put/patch/delete/head/options`), plus context-manager support (`__enter__`/`__exit__`, `close`).
- **`AsyncClient`** (httpx/_client.py:1307) is the parallel async implementation, mirroring `Client`'s method set but with `async def`/`await` (`aclose`, `__aenter__`/`__aexit__`, async `send`, `_send_handling_redirects`, `_send_handling_auth`, `_send_single_request`, async verb methods).

In short: `BaseClient` is the shared abstract core; `Client` and `AsyncClient` are sibling subclasses providing sync vs. async I/O over the same request-building/merging/redirect logic.
